searchText: in general, Nimbus just got its Electra structure in, nothing concrete beyond that (and some minimal stuff related to the engine API updates) Update for **Teku**: - 6110 and 7002 are ready for devnets and in master - We are looking at 7251 and 7549 No issue tracker but we have an Electra label: https://github.com/Consensys/teku/labels/Epic%20Electra Grandine just started to look at all these EIPS What is the general situation of spec-tests for these EIPs? Is there a rough estimate? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3615/files Great progress! Not Pectra interop related, but a general interop - is it OK to ignore the unspec'ed parameters sent to beacon node API? Lodestar VC sends `fee_recipient` when calling https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Validator/produceBlockV3, however, Grandine only accepts requests according to the specification. <@792822129019584562> https://discord.com/channels/945714351841607690/945714351841607694/1225769314649636914 My suggestion would be to not send unspec'ed parameters by default (turn on with flag if it's necessary) because accepting unspec'ed parameters smells undefined behaviour. Yeah, I think by default, unspec'ed params should be ignored, some VC -> BN combos may send/accept additional ones but it is up to them to document that certain VC calls are only compatible with certain BN I see. So you don't see an issue that VC sends unspec'ed parameters and BN just ignores those fields? At Grandine we actually error. Is there any client that errors when it receives unspec'ed parameters? I see a problem when somebody requests BN something and part of the request is just ignored and VC even don't know it. Nimbus also throws an error https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/issues/6636 It's a tricky one, a VC could start sending a new optional field before another BN implements support for it. In that case, do we want the BN to fail to indicate this or proceed as usual just ignoring this field? It's up to clients how they want to handle these compatibility issues that can occur. failing on BN helps to debug, meanwhile, VC could just have this feature optional via CLI flag. I don't like that BN just ignores unknown field, but I'm maybe just too strict here. Today we did another round of BN <> VC compatibility check, and we have made some progress over the past 2 weeks. For all the incompatible client pairs I have created an issue in both CL and VC client's repository. https://github.com/kurtosis-tech/ethereum-package?tab=readme-ov-file#beacon-node--validator-client-compatibility I thought Prysm VC can only connect to Prysm BN because of gRPC? prysm now implemented a flag which supports rest oh awesome! wasn't aware, glad to see we are compatible we send the params which the beacon can perfectly ignore because we added the params considering the other BNs might not apply it, this is to activate extra behavior for lodestar BN so, we interpret the respnse to see if the params were respected or not (so lodestar BN will respond with extra metadata) which the lodestar VC will be able to understand, and a non lodestar VC doesn't need to bother because it wouldn't have asked for non default (spec complaint) response anyway one of the reason to not hide these bind a flag is the validator having using multiple back BNS OK, I think we will allow unspec'ed fields just in this place for now and will review the policy internally later. Not sure what the consensus was, but does it make more sense the first devnet to be 6110, 7002 and 7549 without MaxEB? I am worried MaxEB is a bigger change and it may take a while for clients so it would be good to have an iteration cycle to test well the other EIPs and then can focus on MaxEB?
